stem:
Muttley is an 8-year-old boy with asthma. He has had asthma attacks every month over winter and was discharged from the paediatric intensive care unit a few days ago after a severe attack. He has been off oxygen since yesterday. He has also had a history of waking at night at least 5 days every week, wheeze with exercise, and needs to take his Ventolin at least once a day.

He is now taking salbutamol every 4 hours and is ready for discharge. He weighs 25 kg.

In the asthma action plan, what reliever dose would you write in the “when well” section?
explanation: For a child who is well, the asthma action plan should list salbutamol (Ventolin) as a reliever to be used as needed, typically 2-4 puffs. Regular scheduled dosing is not used in the 'when well' section.
rationale: The question asks for the reliever dose in the 'when well' section of an asthma action plan. Standard advice is salbutamol 2-4 puffs as needed.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is the standard reliever dose when well.
optionExplanations.B: Too high for routine as-needed use when well.
optionExplanations.C: Excessive dose for routine reliever use when well.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because reliever is not given on a regular 12-hour schedule when well.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this is not a standard well-state reliever regimen.
optionExplanations.F: Incorrect because this is far above the usual as-needed dose.
optionExplanations.G: Incorrect because this is too frequent for the 'when well' section.
optionExplanations.H: Incorrect because this is too frequent and too much for routine well-state use.
optionExplanations.I: Incorrect because this is too frequent and excessive for routine well-state use.
